newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 4.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd, Mitsubishi Electric Corp and Texas Instruments Inc have jointly agreed to develop and manufacture one-gigabit dynamic random access memory chips (DRAMs). The companies will equally share development costs, which are expected to be more than 100 billion yen, and patents. They aim to commercialise the products in 1999.

Sapporo Breweries Ltd plans to develop a quality beer barley in Australia for cultivation there in an effort to increase malt imports from the country, in cooperation with the University of Adelaide. They will sign a deal in mid-February, and aim to register the barley in Australia by 2000. Sapporo has consigned improvement of barley varieties to the university since 1992.

K.S. Industry Co Ltd, a Tokyo-based specialised exporter of machinery to Russia, has agreed to provide felling machines and other related equipment worth $100 million to a major Russian lumber company in a barter deal. They will sign a contract in March. Under the agreement, K.S. will export bulldozers, trailers and felling machines from this autumn. The Russian company will pay for the equipment with proceeds from its exports of lumber through eleven trading companies, including Nissho Iwai Corp and Marubeni Corp.

Keyence Corp is expecting to report a record pre-tax profit of nearly 24 billion yen in the year to March, up by more than 20 percent from a year eariler. This is due to the strong sales of sensors used in assembly lines for digital video discs and mobile telecommunications equipment.

JGC Corp is seen to post a pre-tax loss of more than 11 billion yen for the year to March, compared with a forecast of 9.5 billion yen. This is due to the company's failed overseas operations and around two billion yen in estimated appraisal losses on stock holdings given the sharp decline of the stock market.
